rejections.candidate: A dedicated question for the resource or bonus amount on another Player Mat.
rejections.reason: Exposed costs/benefits are already requested by Q03 and action procedures. Different mat quantities are changed quantities, not distinct source rules.

rejections.candidate: Name every ongoing recruit reward by action instead of stating how to obtain the reward from its exposed circle.
rejections.reason: Q12 asks which action determines the ongoing bonus and its resolution; Q44/Q56 directly elicit neighbor-trigger implications. Source pp14/20 defines the exposed circle as the specified reward. Another icon-value enumeration would add routine mat reference detail, not a new trigger, eligibility branch or timing rule.

rejections.candidate: A separate question asking whether bottom coins or a neighbor recruit reward can be declined.

rejections.candidate: Additional lake entry, retreat or river destinations.

rejections.candidate: Spent resources returning to supply, encounter deck-bottom discard or separate ordinary deck shuffles.
rejections.reason: Physical pile/deck handling alone is low-value routine handling under the assigned novelty threshold. Meaningful resource control/payment, deck exhaustion, encounter eligibility/privacy and objective discards are already directly asked.

rejections.candidate: Combat card frequency, power-dial assembly, encounter reference number, achievement-sheet inscriptions, quick-start/sample scoring or Delay of Game.
rejections.reason: Reference/assembly/commemorative/teaching material or explicit optional variant; no qualifying omitted core-play rule.

limitations: This audit uses only the assigned 32-page source and its text; it does not import FAQ, errata, actual objective/encounter/Factory card content or later-edition rules.

Every PDF page text was verified against the fully read extraction; visual inspection focused on the required p19/p29 diagrams and p14/p20 mat/recruit illustrations rather than every decorative image.
PASS means no meaningful source-defined rule/branch/timing gap survived this challenge; coverage does not require a separate test for routine component handling or every mechanical combination.
